title: Graceful Sunset Stages and Customer Experience Matrix for Model Version Deprecations
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Create a repeatable, low-friction deprecation workflow for older model versions that integrates with pinning, published performance profiles, and SDK/console warnings. This ticket defines staged sunset phases, customer-facing notices, in-console migration guidance, programmatic SDK warnings, telemetry to detect migration friction, and an escalation path for enterprise customers. Focus is on minimizing customer downtime and preserving SLAs while enabling runtime capacity management and model catalog hygiene.
background: We host multiple model variants and periodically retire older checkpoints for cost and maintenance reasons. Past retirements exposed gaps: unclear customer communication, lack of automated pin detection, and insufficient telemetry to know why customers fail to migrate. This work builds a formal flow that ties model onboarding (performance profile publication) to an end-of-life lifecycle: staged notices, automatic pin-and-suggest tooling, and clear rollback policies.
goals: Define 4 sunset stages (Notice, Recommended Pin, Forced Pin-Window, Retirement) with timelines and allowed actions
Publish standardized migration guides and per-model migration snippets derived from performance profiles
Add programmatic SDK/CLI warnings and a console banner for pinned routes referencing migration suggestions
Instrument migration telemetry to surface friction hot-spots by customer, SDK version, and route
Create an enterprise handoff path (account manager + dedicated migration runbook) for high-impact customers
out_of_scope: Automated model weight conversion/transformation (handled by model-ops team)
Automated code changes in customer repos — we provide suggestions and diffs only
success_metrics: 95% of non-enterprise customers migrate or pin within 30 days of 'Recommended Pin' stage
<2% unexpected errors (500s/compatibility) attributable to retirement in first 90 days
Time-to-migrate median <= 3 days for customers who follow migration guide
Decrease in manual support tickets related to model deprecations by 60% vs prior run
rollout_plan: Phase 0 - Internal readiness: publish per-model migration guide and compatibility matrix; ENG implements runtime fallback mapping (2 weeks)
Phase 1 - Notice (T-60 days): send customer email + console banner; add 'deprecation' field to model performance profile metadata
Phase 2 - Recommended Pin (T-30 days): console pin suggestion modal, SDK warning logs, auto-attach migration snippet to route details
Phase 3 - Pin Window (T-14 to T-7 days): block new unpinned long-lived routes from using retiring model (soft enforcement) and notify customers
Phase 4 - Retirement (T): model removed from catalog for new requests; existing pinned routes continue for grace period (T+90 days) while archived for auditing
communications: Customer email template (T-60): 'Planned retirement for model X — action recommended: pin to compatible variant or adopt recommended replacement. See migration guide: <link>'
Console banner copy: 'Model X retiring on 2025-04-15. Click for migration steps and one-click pin.'
SDK warning (runtime log): 'DEPRECATION: model=redwood/model-x@v1 will retire on 2025-04-15. See https://redwood.ai/migrate/model-x for migration instructions.'
migration_guidance: Step 1: Identify routes using the retiring model via Console > Routes > Filters (model=redwood/model-x@v1)
Step 2: Review published performance profile and mapped compatible variant (anchor on latency/cost tradeoff)
Step 4: Run smoke tests (sample prompts provided in migration guide) and compare generation scorecards in Console
Step 5: Release and monitor traffic for 48 hours; if issues, rollback to previous pinned variant or open support case
runbook: Operator checklist for retirement day: verify routing fallback rules, ensure archive of model weights, validate observability dashboards for surge in errors
Support triage play: attach migration guide link, escalate to model-ops if output regressions reported
Rollback policy: restore pinned routes to previous variant for customers in the grace window; for non-pinned routes, enable temporary compatible fallback mapping
